land.text: the Oirat homeland on the upper Irtysh that the Torghut and some Dorbets left in 1618

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Oirat Confederation; Nogai Horde'. The Kalmyks page: the Torghut and some Dorbets 'left the upper Irtysh in 1618'; the Oirat page dates the Torghut move 1628 in the text and 1616-17 in the infobox.

land.text: the lower Volga north of the Caspian, 'land that was once part of the Astrakhan Khanate', from which the Oirats expelled the Nogai majority

predecessors.note: 'Upon arrival in the lower Volga region in 1630, the Oirats encamped on land that was once part of the Astrakhan Khanate.' The Nogai page: 'The first group was broken up circa 1632 by the Kalmyks'; 'Conquered by the Kalmyk Khanate: 1634'.

land.text: the Kalmyk steppe between the Volga and the Don, north of the Caspian

successors.note: 'Catherine II abolished the Kalmyk Khanate in October 1771', transferring power to the governor of Astrakhan; the infobox also names the Bukey Horde as a successor (no Cliopatria row, not studied).

correction.text: the lower Volga north of the Caspian where the Oirats arrived in 1630, 58,332 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1630-1631: Cliopatria's first Kalmyk shape begins in 1632, but the infobox gives 'Established by the Oirat Mongols: 1630' and the page 'Upon arrival in the lower Volga region in 1630, the Oirats encamped on land that was once part of the Astrakhan Khanate'. The 1632 outline stands for the two earlier years.

58,332 km2 for 1632-1635 (43.2-47.4 E, 45.5-48.4 N): the lower Volga and the Kalmyk steppe, where the Nogai page has 'The first group was broken up circa 1632 by the Kalmyks' and '1634 major defeat of Nogais by Kalmyks'. The Kalmyk page gives no area figure, so no ratio can be taken.

163,013 km2 for 1636-1737 (41.3-47.4 E, 43.3-48.3 N): the shape nearly triples in 1636 and then stands for 102 years. The Kalmyk page says the khanate 'extended over modern Kalmykia and surrounding areas in the North Caucasus, including Stavropol and Astrakhan' without a date, and the Oirats displaced the Nogai Horde, which 'fled southeast to the northern Caucasian plain and west to the Black Sea steppe'. The 1636 date of the growth, and the edges (Kabardia was attacked in 1644, Astarabad in 1650, Penza raided in 1680, Kuban attacked in 1711: raids, not lands), are unverified: page budget. The Nogai dossier finds the shape holds almost none of the strip Cliopatria takes from the Nogais.

175,318 km2 for 1738-1768, 12,300 km2 larger than the previous shape with the same bbox: unverified: page budget. The Kalmyk page has 'The Kalmyks launch successful campaigns in the Kuban and the Crimea' in 1735 and Cliopatria's Kuban Nogai row ends in 1737 (nogai-horde dossier); no page opened says the Kalmyks kept Kuban land.

174,906 km2 for 1769-1771, the same outline. The Kalmyks page: 'In January 1771' the larger part of the Kalmyks left for Dzungaria under Ubashi Khan (about 169,000 left, about 70,000 arrived); 'Catherine II abolished the Kalmyk Khanate in October 1771'. The shape ends with the khanate.

region.text: the lower Volga north of the Caspian, land once part of the Astrakhan Khanate

ledger.note: 1630: the Oirats arrive on the lower Volga and found the Kalmyk Khanate. 'Upon arrival in the lower Volga region in 1630, the Oirats encamped on land that was once part of the Astrakhan Khanate'; infobox 'Established by the Oirat Mongols: 1630'; first khan Kho Orluk 1633-1644. The Torghut and some Dorbets 'left the upper Irtysh in 1618' (Kalmyks page).

region.text: the strip of the Volga-Yaik steppe (42.3-52.2E, 46.4-48.7N, about 23,000 km2) that Cliopatria's Nogai row drops in 1636, as the nogai-horde dossier draws it

ledger.note: c. 1632: the Kalmyks break the first Nogai group. 'The first group was broken up circa 1632 by the Kalmyks'; 'In the early 17th century, the Horde broke down further under the onslaught of the Kalmyks.' The zone is the one the nogai-horde dossier uses for the same contest.

region.text: the strip of the Volga-Yaik steppe (42.3-52.2E, 46.4-48.7N, about 23,000 km2) that Cliopatria's Nogai row drops in 1636, as the nogai-horde dossier draws it

ledger.note: 1634: the Nogais are defeated. '1634 major defeat of Nogais by Kalmyks'; infobox 'Conquered by the Kalmyk Khanate: 1634'; Kalmyk page: the Oirats 'displaced the Nogai Horde, which fled southeast to the northern Caucasian plain and west to the Black Sea steppe. The remaining nomadic tribes became vassals.' Confidence 2 (reviewer ia-03-d, 2026-10-19): the Nogai page dates the defeat ('1634 major defeat of Nogais by Kalmyks'; infobox 'Conquered by the Kalmyk Khanate: 1634') but names no land; the region is Cliopatria's Small Horde strip.

region.text: the strip of the Volga-Yaik steppe (42.3-52.2E, 46.4-48.7N, about 23,000 km2) that Cliopatria's Nogai row drops in 1636, as the nogai-horde dossier draws it

ledger.note: 1634: the Volga-Yaik steppe passes to the Kalmyks. Infobox of the Nogai page 'Conquered by the Kalmyk Khanate: 1634'. The nogai-horde dossier dates its matching loss 1636, the year Cliopatria drops the strip, and gives the zone the same way. Confidence 2 (reviewer ia-03-d, 2026-10-19): the Nogai page dates the defeat ('1634 major defeat of Nogais by Kalmyks'; infobox 'Conquered by the Kalmyk Khanate: 1634') but names no land; the region is Cliopatria's Small Horde strip.

region.text: the North Caucasus and Kalmyk steppe added in Cliopatria's 1636 shape (about 105,000 km2)

ledger.note: 1636: the Kalmyk shape triples, to the North Caucasus steppe. The Kalmyk page says only that the khanate 'extended over modern Kalmykia and surrounding areas in the North Caucasus, including Stavropol and Astrakhan' (undated); the date 1636 is Cliopatria's. A bridging event: the page is silent on the year and on the former owner (the Nogais fled to the Caucasian plain and the Black Sea steppe).

region.text: the 12,300 km2 added in Cliopatria's 1738 shape, probably Kuban or Terek steppe (unverified)

ledger.note: 1738: the Kalmyk shape grows by about 12,000 km2. A bridging event: the Kalmyk page has 'The Kalmyks launch successful campaigns in the Kuban and the Crimea' (1735) and the Nogai page 'Kalmyks attack Nogais, as agents of Russia' (1693) and '1720s 15,000 Nogai tents flee Kalmyks for Kuban', but gives no land gained in 1738.

region.text: the Kalmyk steppe between the Volga and the Don

ledger.note: October 1771: Catherine II abolishes the Kalmyk Khanate. 'Catherine II abolished the Kalmyk Khanate in October 1771' and the title of Khan; in 'the winter of 1770-1771' (January 1771 on the Kalmyks page) Ubashi Khan led about 169,000 people back to Dzungaria, of whom 'approximately 70,000' arrived. The land passes to the governor of Astrakhan.

wars.name: Kalmyk conquest of the lower Volga

zones.text: the strip of the Volga-Yaik steppe (42.3-52.2E, 46.4-48.7N, about 23,000 km2) that Cliopatria's Nogai row drops in 1636, as the nogai-horde dossier draws it

wars.outcome: The Oirats settle on the lower Volga (1630), break the first Nogai group (c. 1632) and defeat the Nogais (1634); the Nogais flee to the Caucasian plain and the Black Sea steppe.
wars.note: Kalmyk page: a winter campaign against the Astrakhan Tatars in 1635; 1643 'Kalmyks push back from Astrakhan' (Nogai page).

wars.name: Kalmyk campaigns in the North Caucasus and Kuban
wars.outcome: Raids and Russian-allied campaigns without a dated frontier: Kabardia 1644, Astarabad 1650, Crimea and Nogais 1658, the Kuban attack of 1711 (20,474 Kalmyks and 4,100 Russians; 11,460 Nogais killed) and campaigns in the Kuban and Crimea in 1735.
wars.note: Ayuka Khan (1672-1724) made the Kazakhs and Turkmen tributaries and fought Dagestanis, Kumyks, Kabardians and Kuban forces (Ayuka Khan page); no land changes hands on the pages.

wars.name: Kalmyk exodus of 1771
wars.outcome: About 169,000 Kalmyks left the Volga for Dzungaria in January 1771 and about 70,000 arrived; the khanate was abolished in October.
wars.note: Kalmyk page: the ice on the Volga weakened and only those on the east bank could leave.

certainty.note: A nomad khanate on the open steppe between the Russian settlements and the Caspian; no page gives a boundary line, and Russia's frontier with it is not described.

sources.note: The Nogais and the Kalmyks: 'circa 1632', '1634 major defeat', 1693, 1711, 1720s, infobox 'Conquered by the Kalmyk Khanate: 1634'.

sources.title: Ayuka Khan
sources.note: Reign 1672-1690 as taishi and 1690-1724 as khan; service to Russia; campaigns. Silent on treaties and lands.

notes:
Cliopatria row reviewed: Kalmyk Khanate (1632-1771, 4 shapes). The dossier starts in 1630 (infobox and page) and adds a new keyframe for 1630-1631.

Unverified (page budget, and the pages are silent): the 1636 growth from 58,332 to 163,013 km2 and the 1738 growth by 12,300 km2 are recorded as confidence-1 gains from 'nobody' and are the researcher's bridge; the khanate's boundaries with Russia (the Yaik, Volga-Don and Terek lines) are on no page opened. The Russian oaths and treaties (1655, 1657, 1661, 1673 in the usual accounts) are on none of the four pages, so the Kalmyk Khanate's status as a Russian client (rule 4, lighter tint of Russia) has no event here; the tsardom-of-russia and russian-empire dossiers should open a page for it. Capital: the infobox gives 'Ayuka Khan's residence (1697-1724)' and no place, so identity.capitals is empty. Rulers: the pages give only fragments (Kho Orluk 1633-1644 first khan, Ayuka 1672-1724, Ubashi 1761-1771 last), so no ruler strip.

Matching counterparts: the nogai-horde dossier has the contest (1632-1634) over the same Volga-Yaik strip but dates its matching loss 1636, the year of Cliopatria's shape change, while this dossier dates the gain 1634 (infobox of the Nogai page). Tsardom/Russian Empire: the 1771 land passes to the Russian Empire (Astrakhan governor); the astrakhan-khanate dossier marks Cliopatria's Astrakhan rows of 1642-1768 wrong (they are the Don Cossacks outline), so the neighbour list in the seed is not evidence of a border.

Infobox area: none given. The Bukey Horde, named as a successor in the infobox, has no Cliopatria row and was not studied. Pages: four opened.
